description.narrative: Cost and time of compliance with trade procedures reduced

Time and cost to cross project BCPs reduced by 30% (2014 baseline: Altanbulag BCP: 4.8 hours, $659; Bichigt BCP: 3.7 hours, $660; and Zamiin-Uud BCP: 8.7 hours, $383) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The average time and cost to cross project borders have steadily declined since 2014. According to the CAREC CPMM annual report for 2016, the performance of the project BCPs show varying signs of improvement as follows: Altanbulag BCP: 4.7 hours; Bichigt BCP: 1.6 hour; and Zamiin-Uud BCP: 5.2 hours, $110. Data Source: CAREC CPMM quarterly and annual reports
CAREC TSCC and CCC annual reports
GACT semiannual reports Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity of relevant border agencies improved Indicator: 200 trained participants reflecting a gender balance in line with the composition of the workforce, reported on improved gender sensitive and coordinated border management, risk management, training management, performance management, advance ruling, and time release study skills by 2027 Progress/Status: Capacity building needs assessment was carried out by the Capacity Development Specialist and some trainings have been conducted in 2023. Elaboration of the Curricula by 10 project trainers on the topics covering Coordinated Border Management, IPR, E-commerce, RM, PCA, Customs Operational Practices for Enforcement and Seizures and SEW was launched and completed in Q4 2023. Technical trainings on SEW implementation was organized to SEW stakeholders in March 2024. Even project target has been achieved, the project team is planning to conduct more capacity building activities until project completion. A total of 250 participants attended the trainings conducted by the consultant and 53 trainers were trained during its contracting period. The elaboration of the Curricula by 11 project trainers on the 10 was completed and handled to the relevant authorities during the workshop on “Coordinated Border Management and Human capital” dated 24 May 2024. Data Source: Self-assessment and feedback report from participants Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: y

Output: Communication infrastructure for CAIS improved and MCGA system made interoperable. Indicator: 2a. CAIS functional requirements developed and operational (2010 baseline: basic application development) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: CAIS functional requirements developed. The consultant's contract has been extended until 1 May 2022 due to the COVID-19 outbreak related delays. "The Capacity Development of users of CAIS" is approved by the MCGA. All required equipment for the upgraded CAIS system have been procured and handed over to MCGA in Q2 2019 and Q3 2021. The "Performance Certificate" certifying the completion and acceptance of work packages carried out under the consulting services were submitted as an attachment to the official letter dated 26 April 2022 issued by the MCGA.
Testing and introduction of CAIS system improvements and relevant training are carried out in Custom houses and branches. Data Source: 2a.Quarterly progress reports from ICT firm
Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2028 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Communication infrastructure for CAIS improved and MCGA system made interoperable. Indicator: 2b. MCGA system seamlessly exchange information (2014 baseline: no automated information exchange) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: MCGA system/CAIS will seamlessly exchange information with other government agencies' systems through the government's data exchange platform "Khur" and "E-Mongolia" platform starting from Q4 2021. CAIS upgrade work has been completed. Data Source: 2b.MCGA semiannual report
Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2028 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Facilities and equipment at BCPs upgraded and improved Indicator: 1a. Civil works completed with the required Universal Standard Facilities (to cater to PWD, elderly and nursing mothers) by 2027 (2014 baseline: 0) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Civil works' contracts are progressing at various levels: (i) rehabilitating the Altanbulag BCP is cleared by the State Commission on 7 July 2025, (ii) construction of Single Stop Service Center at Sukhbaatar BCP is completed, (iii) construction of a 1.7km road connecting Altanbulag BCP is completed, (iv) rehabilitation of Borshoo BCP is completed, (v) Borshoo BCP road and utility connection is completed; (vi) construction of Bichigt BCP road and utility connection stands at 35%; and (vii) construction of Bichigt BCP facilities stands at 10% with no tangible progresses have been made since 2023. Due to unsatisfactory performance of the CW6 contractor, the contract was terminated. The re-bidding of the package is due soon. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from contractors
Updates to CAREC annual SOM and Ministerial Conference Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Facilities and equipment at BCPs upgraded and improved Indicator: 1b. Needed equipment installed at project BCPs by 2027 (2014 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: BCP equipment have partially been procured and installed at the project BCPs. Re-bidding of remaining procurement packages completed and installation of the remaining equipment is in progress. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from contractors
Updates to CAREC annual SOM and Ministerial Conference Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2028 Target value: Y

Output: Facilities and equipment at BCPs upgraded and improved Indicator: 1c. merged with 1a Progress/Status: This indicator is on track to meet target. The reason to merge this with 1a was it's technically impossible to establish separate lanes for inspection of women traders. Thus, during preparation of the additional financing project it's proposed to merge the target with more implementable and practical target indicator of an Universal Standard Facilities (cater to PWD, elderly, and nursing mothers), which are part of the designs of the BCP facilities. (2019 baseline: no single electronic window system exists) Progress/Status: The recruitment of the consulting firm to develop the SEW system is planned to be initiated in Q1 2026. Terms of Reference of the consulting firm has been updated to reflect comments from WG members. Output: Preparatory work for single-window system undertaken Indicator: Institutional arrangements in place and operational. Progress/Status: The MCGA and Foreign Investment and Foreign Trade Agency are appointed as the lead agencies to implement FTSEW system by the order 178 of the Government on 17 May 2023. The Ministry of Economy and Development has established a WG composed of all relevant ministries and agencies, which have been working effectively to expedite implementation of FTSEW and preparing a work plan covering 2023-2025.
